_comment: Filling the box. Shapeless on purpose (Jonah, 2026-09-05): how you arrange tools in a toolbox is not
a thing the world should have an opinion about, only whether you have them. What is shaped is
building the box.
A real field kit, each part mapped to something that already exists rather than to an invented
intermediate. Three of them are instruments -- a brush to dust a specimen, a streak plate to scratch
it against, a lodestone for the magnetic test -- and four are REFERENCE SPECIMENS, the known minerals
you hold an unknown one against: diamond for hardness at the top of the scale, nether quartz,
amethyst, and an echo shard.
The four are deliberately from four different worlds (Jonah, 2026-09-07): the overworld, the Nether,
a geode and the deep dark. A kit that spans everywhere already reachable is the right shape for an
instrument whose whole job is naming what is in a place nobody has been.
The streak plate is temperstone, which a hot Age standing in lava bakes out of its own ground -- so
the instrument that tells you what an Age holds is itself built from something only a written Age can
give you. The rime crystal that stood here goes to the crystal viewer, where a crystal is the thing
itself rather than a stand-in for a hand lens.
Two things came OUT on 2026-09-07. Deretheni, because 7.7 makes it the midgame material and an
early-game instrument must not gate on one. And the barrel, because the toolbox is already the thing
you keep samples in -- a box inside a box was the kit describing its own container twice.
Scorched temperstone stood here briefly and went too: two of one family read as a shortcut, and the
byproduct is wanted for the grinder's gunpowder route instead.
